description: We are a team of curious and enthusiastic individuals passionate about space, technology, and innovation. We enjoy exploring challenging problems and turning creative ideas into meaningful solutions. We are looking for like-minded teammates interested in coding, research, data analysis, design, and space science who are eager to learn, collaborate, and build something impactful together
summary:
SPHEREx Blink is a web-based tool that helps users explore SPHEREx observations and look for objects that may move or change in brightness over time. Instead of opening and comparing astronomical images one by one, users can view multiple targets together in one place.

Users can search by object name or sky coordinates, compare up to nine targets, and play observations in synchronized or independent modes. They can also view image differences, mark possible moving sources, and export measurements in JSON or CSV format.

We built the application using Python, FastAPI, Astropy, NumPy, and SciPy, connecting to NASA's IRSA archive to retrieve and align SPHEREx image cutouts. An offline demo is also included to explore the interface without real observations.

Our aim is to make the search for changing or moving objects easier and more accessible, while helping users identify candidates for further scientific investigation.
details:
We developed SPHEREx Blink to make it easier to spot objects that may move or change in brightness across astronomical images. Normally, comparing observations from different dates means opening and checking images one by one. Our tool brings them together in a single view.

Users can search by object name or sky coordinates, browse available observations, compare up to nine targets, and play images together or separately. They can also mark possible moving sources and export their measurements as JSON or CSV files.

We built it using Python, FastAPI, Astropy, NumPy, and SciPy, with a browser-based interface. One feature we focused on was making comparisons easier through aligned images, playback controls, and difference views. We also included an offline demo so users can explore the features without connecting to IRSA.

SPHEREx Blink is an exploration tool, helping users find interesting candidates for further scientific investigation.
